core.title: SMOKE must drive the real entry point, not a synthetic fixture
core.given: A SMOKE-phase test of the agent launch / production wiring is planned (in a plan or acceptance artifact), written or modified.
core.when: Choosing what the SMOKE test drives as its primary production wiring.
core.then: The SMOKE test must drive the application's real launch entry point — the real entry surfaces, which exercise real command construction and the real launch path — not a synthetic stand-in (a stub process, a test double for the real wiring, or an embedded agent-script constant) as its primary production wiring.
prefer: Launch the real entry point the way production launches it, so real command construction and the real launch path are exercised.
Write agent scripts to temporary files.
avoid: A test double for the real wiring component as the SMOKE test's production wiring (it bypasses the real dispatch path).
A trivial stub process as the command under test (it exercises only a wrapper or the process lifecycle, not real command construction).
Agent scripts embedded as string constants.
Treating a green SMOKE suite as proof when it only proves the harness.
unless: An inline, dated suppression of this rule; the debt expires on that date.
core.why: A stubbed SMOKE test proves the harness, not the product, and is green precisely where real wiring is untested. Incident #854: a real defect in the launch command stayed invisible because the SMOKE tests drove a stub that never exercised the real command-construction path.
evidence: The SMOKE test invokes the real launch entry point (the real entry surfaces bound in the profile), exercising real command construction and the real launch path.
No synthetic stand-in (a test double for the real wiring, a stub process, or an embedded agent-script constant) appears as primary wiring in SMOKE tests, unless under an unexpired dated suppression.
Agent scripts are written to temporary files rather than embedded as string constants.
verification: Scope: SMOKE-phase tests and the plan or acceptance artifacts that specify them. Non-SMOKE unit and integration tests that use test doubles or stub processes to isolate a component do not fire.

The check flags synthetic stand-ins — a test double for the real wiring, a stub process standing in for the real command, an embedded agent-script constant — used as primary wiring in a SMOKE-phase test; the exact banned-fixture list belongs to the stack's realization of this rule.

Compliant driving forms are the stack's real entry surfaces (bound in the profile at the launch-surface idiom, proposed as idiom.launch_surface) invoked through their production path; the stack's concrete invocation forms and helpers belong to the realization.
Suppression is an inline, time-boxed marker in the stack's syntax (enforcement.suppression_marker); the debt expires on the stated date, and expired suppressions do not suppress.

fires: A SMOKE-phase acceptance or plan artifact specifies a test that drives a test double or a stub process instead of the real launch entry point.
A SMOKE-phase test is written or modified so it launches an inline stub command or an embedded synthetic agent script as the agent command.
An existing SMOKE test proves the launch path only via a trivial stub process.
doesNotFire: Unit or integration (non-SMOKE) tests that use a test double or stub process to isolate a component.
A SMOKE test that drives the real launch entry point and writes agent scripts to temporary files.
A SMOKE test carrying a valid, unexpired dated inline suppression for this rule.

neutralityNotes: The obligation is fully stack-neutral: a SMOKE-phase test must drive the real launch entry point, not a synthetic stand-in. What could not be made neutral: (1) the banned-fixture enumeration (FakeMultiplexer, Popen of cat/sleep/python -c, _SYNTHETIC_AGENT) and the accepted invocation forms (subprocess.run([sys.executable, -m, atdd.cli, ...]), invoke_atdd_spawn) are detector data of this rule's realization, delivered as bunOnly, not profile data; (2) the real entry surfaces (atdd spawn / atdd coach / rendered launch prompt) are a rule-relevant launch-surface idiom, not boundary artifact kinds, so a new key idiom.launch_surface is proposed and used pending owner approval; (3) tmp_path binds to the proposed idiom.temporary_file; the core says only 'agent scripts to temporary files' — the temporary-file/embedded-constant obligation is scoped to agent scripts, matching Bun, and does not cover unrelated script inputs; (4) the plan-artifact name (WMBT) binds to roles.plan_artifact.kinds; (5) the suppression syntax binds to enforcement.suppression_marker — only the expiry semantics are core; (6) activation facts carry no note field in the core schema — the notes are observer-design guidance, and facts[4]'s note (concrete detector fixtures) is preserved as bunOnly; (7) per-rule severity and disposition are core verification, not bunOnly and not profile keys. 'SMOKE', acceptance and plan-artifact roles, and product vocabulary (agent, agent script, launch path, command construction, dispatch) are convention/product terms, not stack terms, and were kept in the core.
